pamphlet_excerpts: Here Basic Safety: Here are some basic safety precautions; there are more safety suggestions later in this pamphlet.
Read Work Requirements: As you read this pamphlet and work on the requirements, payattention to safety and see whether you can add to this list.
Requirement Study Chapter: For requirement 2, study the chapter called “Schematic Diagrams.” You may choose a schematic diagram from thispamphlet, then copy it carefully.
Drawingmust Show Resistors: Your drawingmust show resistors, capacitors, and transistors or integratedcircuits.
step_by_step_procedure: Correct Symbols Components: Use the correct symbols for these components, label all parts, and be prepared to tell the purpose of eachcomponent.
Show Drawing Tellwhat: Show your drawing to your counselor and tellwhat you have learned.
Requirement Learn Solder: For requirement 3, learn how to solder and then practicesoldering and desoldering wires.
Show Soldering Skills: When you think you areready, show your soldering skills to your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Poor Connections Crystalline: Poor connections look crystalline andgrainy, or the solder tends to blob.
Pull Slightly Wire: After the solder is well set, pull slightly on the wire to seewhether it is a good, tight connection.
Case Accidentally Wrong: In case you accidentally make a wrong connection or have tomove a component that has been placed incorrectly, you shouldlearn how to desolder.
Care Desolderingto Avoid: Take care when desolderingto avoid breaking or destroying good parts.
step_by_step_procedure: Leads Oncomponents Resistors: The leads oncomponents such as resistors or transistors and the lugs onother parts might sometimes break off when desoldering a good, tight.
Care Indesoldering Delicate: To avoid heat damage, use as much care indesoldering delicate parts as you do in soldering them.
Usuallyeasiest Way Metal: The first and usuallyeasiest way is to use a metal wick or braid on a small dispenserreel to remove the melted solder.
Braid Available: This braid is available at mostelectronics parts stores.

pamphlet_excerpts: Here Basic Safety: Here are some basic safety precautions; there are more safety suggestions later in this pamphlet.
Read Work Requirements: As you read this pamphlet and work on the requirements, payattention to safety and see whether you can add to this list.
Requirement Study Chapter: For requirement 2, study the chapter called “Schematic Diagrams.” You may choose a schematic diagram from thispamphlet, then copy it carefully.
Drawingmust Show Resistors: Your drawingmust show resistors, capacitors, and transistors or integratedcircuits.
step_by_step_procedure: Correct Symbols Components: Use the correct symbols for these components, label all parts, and be prepared to tell the purpose of eachcomponent.
Show Drawing Tellwhat: Show your drawing to your counselor and tellwhat you have learned.
Requirement Learn Solder: For requirement 3, learn how to solder and then practicesoldering and desoldering wires.
Show Soldering Skills: When you think you areready, show your soldering skills to your counselor.

requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Show how to solve a simple problem involving current, voltage, and resistance using Ohm's law. (b) Tell about the need for and the use of test equipment in electronics. Name three types of test equipment. Tell how they operate. (c) Demonstrate to your counselor how to read the colored bands of a resistor to determine its resistance value. (d) Explain the differences between Through Hole and Surface Mount assembly technologies and give three advantages of each.

pamphlet_excerpts: Electronic Test Equipment: Electronic Test Equipment METER MOVEMENT 1mA, + SHUNT Schematic of an ammeter Schematic of an ammeter Voltmeter.
Voltmeter Designed Measure: The voltmeter is designed to measure voltage anduses the same type of meter movement as an ammeter.
Thevoltmeter Connected: Thevoltmeter is connected across the voltage to be measured.
Tomeasure Voltage Points: Tomeasure voltage between two points, touch the negative leadto the more negative point and the positive lead to the morepositive point.
step_by_step_procedure: Circuit Test Not: The circuit under test need not be broken orinterfered with in any way.
Low Voltage Applied: A low voltage can be applied directly to the meter movement.
Higher Voltage However: A higher voltage, however, might cause a high enoughcurrent to burn out the delicate coil.
Reason Largevalue Resistor: For this reason, a largevalue resistor is connected in series with the meter movement.

pamphlet_excerpts: Electronics Industry Several: The electronics industry has several general areas with manytypes of careers available in each area.
Areas Includemanufacturing: These areas includemanufacturing, merchandising, operating, servicing ormaintaining, and engineering electronic parts and equipment.
Positionsrequire College: Some positionsrequire a college degree, while a degree from a vocationalschool is adequate for othercareers.
Companiesallow On-the-job: Some companiesallow on-the-job training, but almost all require at least a high school diploma.
step_by_step_procedure: Electronics Manufacturing: In electronics manufacturing, most positions are in factories.
Occupations Include: Occupations include assemblers, that is, the people who helpbuild electronic equipment.
Ahigh School Education: Ahigh school education is neededas well as mechanical aptitude.
Merchandising Sales Field: Merchandising, or sales, is another field for thoseinterested in electronics.
